html:
SMTO-EML-0019 — Your email's subject or file name can't be used

GUID: 57c8ad78-4ba8-538d-89e4-4b885155a14a
Slug: email-header-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The subject line or an attachment's file name has a hidden character, such as a line break, or is too long. SMTO stopped before sending, so nothing went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the subject on a single line with no line breaks or tabs, and well under 998 characters. A line break in the subject could change how the email is read, so SMTO refuses it.
  2. If you attached a file, make sure its name is under 255 characters with no line breaks. Rename it and add it again with Add context if needed. Attachment names follow the same rules as the subject line.
  3. Ask SMTO to send the email again. Nothing was sent, so sending the corrected email won't create a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. This is about how the email was written, not your email account, so don't change your password or reconnect the account because of it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Header validation rejected the subject or an attachment filename because it was not a string, contained control characters (such as CR or LF), or exceeded its length limit.

What this means

  • An email header has invalid characters or exceeds its supported length. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • Header validation rejects control characters or excessive length.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Check the field fact (subject, or header for an attachment filename). header() rejects non-string values, any character below 0x20 or equal to 0x7F, and values over the limit (998 characters for the subject, 255 for filenames); strip CR, LF and other control characters and shorten the value.
  • Correct the indicated header; remove control characters and respect its length limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected header passes validation.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
